android.desc:
* THIS IS A DEVELOPER TOOL ONLY *
* If you have problem with your media app, contact that app's support *
* For install / uninstall issues, please contact Google Play Support at  https://support.google.com/googleplay/ *

This app will display the information of the Digital Right Management (DRM) module from Android Media Framework and MediaDrm API.

This app only shows the info, and is not doing any test on the availability. 

Popular media apps rely on DRM and HDCP for content protection. However, they may also implement additional limitation such as whitelist or blacklist. Please contact that media app, not this app, if you have any difficulty on their app.

Ads revenue of this app is used for paying the Ads Network so you could find this app easier.

This app currently support the following DRM module (will display only when supported)
- CENC ClearKey
- Adobe Primetime
- Google Widevine Modular DRM
- Marlin 
- Microsoft PlayReady
- Verimatrix
- Wiseplay DRM

This app usually update twice a month, for updating the underlying libraries from AndroidX and Firebase. These changes are invisible to most users.

This app is Free, sponsor me at https://github.com/sponsors/seventhmoon

To learn more, you may visit the following links which mentioned about this app.
- https://www.ghacks.net/2016/12/03/check-your-android-devices-drm-capabilities/
- https://android.gadgethacks.com/how-to/check-if-your-phone-can-stream-hd-video-from-netflix-amazon-prime-video-other-services-0181603/
- https://hometheatrelife.com/check-drm-info-android/
- https://www.cnx-software.com/2015/11/16/drm-info-android-app-reports-widevine-and-playready-drm-information/
- https://www.androidauthority.com/widevine-explained-821935/
- http://www.androidpolice.com/2017/12/10/oneplus-5-5t-cant-play-netflix-hd-feature-will-added-point/

quotes.text:
Widevine is supported on Android, and is utilized by the MediaDrm APIs.[1][2]

Netflix uses Google’s SafetyNet API to make sure the device is “certified”. When this API check returns false, some features (like downloading media for offline viewing) will be disabled for the device. In some cases, the app won’t even show up in Google Play. Devices with a custom ROM are likely to fail the test, but luckily the check can be circumvented with the hide feature of Magisk[3]. Netflix works fine on my LineageOS-powered device when using Magisk.

But even if your device passes the SafetyNet checks, you might not be able to play HD videos. This depends on the Widevine security level, which can be L1, L2 or L3; only devices with L1 are allowed to play HD videos. You can check your device’s Widevine security level with DRM Info[4], for example. Netflix also lists specific device models and chipsets for which they support HD streaming.[5]

[1] https://source.android.com/devices/drm

[2] https://developer.android.com/reference/android/media/MediaDrm

[3] https://github.com/topjohnwu/Magisk

[4] https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.androidfung.drminfo

[5] https://help.netflix.com/en/node/23939
